information  for  citizens  to  secure  access  to  information  under  the  control  of  public  authorities, 
in  order  to  promote  transparency  and  accountability  in  the  working  of  every  public  authority, 
and  whereas  the  attached  publication  of  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  is  of  particular  interest 
to  the  public,  particularly  disadvantaged  communities  and  those  engaged  in  the  pursuit  of 
education  and  knowledge,  the  attached  public  safety  standard  is  made  available  to  promote  the 
timely  dissemination  of  this  information  in  an  accurate  manner  to  the  public.

IS  :  5425  (  Part  4  )  -  1987 

Indian  Standard 

METHODS  OF 
CHEMICAL  ANALYSIS   OF  MISCH  METAL 

PART  4     DETERMINATION  OF  ALUMINIUM 

0.    FOREWORD 

0.1  This  Indian  Standard  (  Part  4  )  was  adopted  by  Indian  Standards 
Institution  on  16  January  1987,  after  the  draft  finalized  by  the  Methods 
of  Chemical  Analysis  of  Non-Ferrous  Metals  Sectional  Committee  had 
been  approved  by  the  Structural  and  Metals  Division  Council. 

0.2  Misch  metal  is  an  alloy  of  rare  earth  metals  and  is  used  for  improving 
the  strength,  fluidity  and  other  properties  of  cast  iron,  steel,  aluminium, 
magnesium  and  nickel  alloys  to  which  it  is  added.  Chemical  analysis  of 
misch  metal  is  covered  in  parts.  In  this  part,  a  method  for  determination 
of  aluminium  has  been  covered.    Other  parts  are: 

Part  1  Determination  of  cerium 

Part  2  Determination  of  rare  earths 

Part  3  Determination  of  iron 

Part  5  Determination  of  carbon 

0.3  In  reporting  the  result  of  a  test  or  analysis  made  in  accordance  with 
this  standard;  if  the  final  value,  observed  or  calculated,  is  to  be  rounded 
off,  it  shall  be  done  in  accordance  with  IS  :  2-1960*. 


1.  SCOPE 

1.1  This  Indian  Standard  (  Part  4  )  covers  the  method  for  determination 
of  aluminium  in  misch  metal  as  specified  in  IS  :  4182-1967f- 

2.  QUALITY  OF  REAGENTS 

2.1  Unless  specified   otherwise,   analytical   grade  reagents  and  distilled 
water  (  see  IS  :  1070-1977J  )  shall  be  employed  in  the  test. 


♦Rules  for  rounding  off  numerical  values  (  revised  ). 

fSpecification  for  misch  metal. 

{Specification  for  water,  for  general  laboratory  use  {second  revision  ). 


IS  :  5425  (  Part  4  )  -  1987 

3,  DETERMINATION  OF  ALUMINIUM  BY 
SPECTROPHOTOMETRIC  METHOD 

3.1  Outline  of  the  Method  —  Aluminium  is  extracted  as  its  oxinate  at 
pH  5*0  keeping  iron  complexed  with  O-phenanthroline.  The  absorbance 
of  the  extracted  aluminium  oxinate  is  measured  at  395  nm. 

3.2  Reagents 

3.2.1  Dilute  Hydrochloric  Acid  —  1:1  (  v/v  ). 

3.2.2  Hydroxylamine  Hydrochloride  —  Dissolve  10  g  of  the  reagent 
in  100  ml  water. 

3.2.3  O-phenanthroline  —  Dissolve  1  g  of  the  reagent  in  a  litre  of  water. 

3.2.4  Acetate  Buffer  —  Mix  70  ml  of  sodium  acetate  solution  (0*2  M  ) 
with  30  ml  acetic  acid  (  0  2  M  ). 

3.2.5  Oxine  Solution  —  Dissolve  0'5  g  in  50  ml  of  chloroform  as  and 
when  required. 

3.2.6  Standard  Aluminium  Solution — Dissolve  0'500  g  of  cleaned 
aluminium  foil  (  purity  =  99*9  percent  )  in  25  ml  dilute  hydrochloric 
acid  (  1:1  ).  Evaporate  it  to  dryness  on  a  water  bath.  Add  1  ml  of 
concentrate  hydrochloric  acid  (  rd  =  1*16  )  and  make  up  the  volume  to 
500  ml  with  water.  (  TO  ml  contains  TO  mg  of  Al  ).  This  solution 
is  further  diluted  as  and  when  required  to  give  10  ft  g  of  Al/ml. 

3.3  Procedure 

3.3.1  Weigh  2'000  g  of  the  sample  into  a  beaker.  Add  50  ml  of  dilute 
hydrochloric  acid  and  dissolve  the  sample.  Make  up  the  volume  to 
200  ml  in  a  volumetric  flask. 

3.3.2  Take  1*0  ml  of  the  sample  solution  from  3.3.1  in  a  beaker  and 
add  5  ml  of  hydroxylamine-hydrochloride  and  20  ml  of  a  O-phenanthro- 
line. Adjust  the  pHto  4*0  and  transfer  the  solution  to  a  100-ml 
separating  funnel. 

3.3.3  Add  10  ml  of  buffer  followed  by  10*0  ml  of  oxine  solution. 

3.3.4  Shake  for  3  minutes,  run  the  chloroform  extract  into  a  small 
stoppered  dry  flask  containing  1  g  of  anhydrous  sodium  sulphate  and 
shake  to  remove  the  droplet  of  water. 

3.3.5  Measure  the  absorbance  of  chloroform  solution  at  395  nm 
against  a  reagent  blank  prepared  by  following  3.3.1  to  3.3.4. 

3.3.6  Take  aliquots  of  standard  aluminium  solution  and  follow 
3.3.2  to  3.3.5.  Plot  the  absorbance  against  the  amount  of  aluminium 
taken. 


IS  :  5425  (  Part  4  )  -  1987 
3.4  Calculation 

Aluminium,  percent  =  ~j^t 

where 

M  =  mass  of  aluminium  in   /xg   obtained  from  the  calibration 
graph.
